C1.reason: It names who decides and what happens either way, although the word improves still needs the number that C5 asks for.

C2.reason: Change, metric and direction are all there.

C3.reason: The coin is tossed per notice. A holder with three permits can get the reminder for one and not for another, so one person sits in both arms.

C4.reason: Two primary metrics, with the choice left until the data are in. That is a second chance at a win.

C5.reason: Any improvement is not a number. Without one there is no sample size and no line between a result worth acting on and noise.

C6.reason: One guardrail with no threshold and no action. Keeping an eye on it stops nothing.

C7.reason: Stopping at the first significant day is peeking. The false-win rate is far above 5%.

C8.reason: Ten days cover one whole week and part of another, and no month-end. The size has no stated source because there is no minimum effect.

C9.reason: The test is chosen after the data are seen. Nothing says which unit is analysed or that holders are analysed as assigned.

C10.reason: Both checks are planned before the result is read.

C11.reason: Arms and the reason for withholding are stated, but no guardrail protects any group of holders from harm.

C12.reason: Fields, pseudonymised keys and aggregate reporting are stated. A retention date would make it better.
